title: Outlook and Teams down: the Microsoft 365 outage, hour by hour
dek: What broke, when (in India time), what Microsoft has said, and what still works.
bigLabel: Roughly how long from the first reports (≈ 11:30 pm IST, 12 Nov) to Microsoft saying service health was restored (evening, 13 Nov IST)

glance.what: From late on 12 November (India time), Microsoft's Exchange Online servers failed, taking down Outlook and parts of Teams, SharePoint and Copilot in 74 countries and territories for about a day. Microsoft says a problem introduced during an earlier network capacity upgrade surfaced after a recent network change, and that it was not a cyber attack.
glance.why: Microsoft 365 runs email and meetings for millions of companies, schools and government offices, including in India. Courts lost live feeds and Australian agencies were hit.
glance.next: Microsoft reports broad recovery and has apologised. Its full incident report should give more detail on what went wrong.

forYou: Outlook and Teams should be working again. Emails sent during the outage may arrive late as queues clear. If something still fails, restart the app or sign out and back in.

events.title: Microsoft starts investigating email problems
events.summary: Shortly before 1 pm US Eastern time, Microsoft says it is investigating reports of users unable to reach Exchange Online mailboxes in the Americas. It soon says users in any region could be affected.

events.title: Outage spreads across Microsoft 365
events.summary: Microsoft opens a wider incident at 1:26 pm ET: customers may be unable to connect to Exchange Online, Teams, SharePoint, Copilot and Defender XDR. Outlook problem reports on Downdetector reach about 130,000.

events.title: A first fix brings some servers back
events.summary: Microsoft says it has validated a different way of running server health checks, bringing some servers back online. It says it has found no recent change linked to the start of the problem; its investigation points to a component that processes server health checks.

events.title: Restored servers fail again
events.summary: Microsoft says servers it returned to service can become unresponsive again once they receive traffic. It pauses deployments, limits some traffic to the affected systems and keeps restarting servers.

events.title: No sustained recovery yet; not a cyber attack
events.summary: As Europe wakes up, the outage is still widespread. Microsoft says its fixes are bringing partial recovery but not a sustained one, and a Microsoft executive says it was not caused by a cyber attack. No time is given for a full fix.

events.title: 'Encouraging recovery progress'
events.summary: Microsoft says service availability and email delivery are improving across a growing share of affected systems, after restarting servers and redirecting traffic. Some users report regaining access.

events.title: Microsoft: service restored
events.summary: Microsoft says its fixes have restored service health and functionality, and that email queues are approaching normal levels. It repeats there is no sign of a cyber attack.

events.title: What caused it: early explanations
events.summary: Microsoft has traced the trouble to an overloaded process on affected servers that sets up secure connections, which caused them to fail health checks. The Verge's Tom Warren reports it is linked to an Azure network (VNET) configuration change, and Australia's Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke says Microsoft told him it was related to a software update. Microsoft has not confirmed a root cause and has promised a post-incident report.
events.differs: Microsoft describes overloaded servers; The Verge points to a network configuration change; Australia's minister cites a software update. These may be parts of the same chain, but Microsoft has not confirmed which started it.

events.title: Microsoft names a cause and apologises
events.summary: In an updated statement, Microsoft says the incident "was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change", and that it was a technical issue not related to cyber attacks or AI agents. It says it is "deeply sorry", reports broad recovery, and says it will give a fuller explanation in a full incident report. Downdetector data showed services hit in 74 countries and territories.
